text:
incident-bot: P0 ALERT — Elevated 5xx rate and median latency in eu-west (region). Paging oncall @maya and ops @sam. Alerts: errors > 3% for 10m, p95 latency > 900ms.

maya: saw it, joining. I’m oncall for eu-west.

sam: looking. initial graphs show traffic shift around 02:11Z, error spikes concentrated on provider-b endpoints.

ryan: same. stacktrace-ish from runtime: 
```
2026-03-15T02:10:55Z ERROR inference: kvcache mismatch, provider-b gpu OOM-ish fallback, code 502
2026-03-15T02:11:02Z WARN router: stream reset by upstream provider-b
```

alex: note: provider-b recently pushed a cuda driver rollback to a subset of nodes in eu-west yesterday. Could be related.

leah: support queue: 12+ customers reporting increased latencies and failed completions. Top affected: voxly-prod, quicksheet-enterprise, chatly. All in eu-west.

maya: quick triage: can we soft-divert new requests to provider-a for eu-west while preserving sticky sessions? Prefer no full region failover yet.

sam: we can do a provider reroute at the edge for non-pinned routes. Plan: 1) rate-limit non-SLA tiers to 30rps, 2) reroute new sessions to provider-a, 3) partial brownout (disable non-essential features like long-context and reranking) to reduce upstream load.

ryan: agree. adding: enable prefix-KV cache warming for provider-a to avoid cold-start latencies. Also set autoretry policy backoff to 200ms to avoid thundering herd.

maya: executing runbook step 1: apply quota change for non-SLA tenants.

ops-bot: Command executed: `redwood quota update --region eu-west --tier standard --max-rps 30`
ops-bot: Result: OK. Affected tenants: ~420, enforcement active in 15s.

leah: already seeing fewer complaints from standard-tier devs. Enterprise customers still at full throughput.

sam: step 2: re-route new requests from provider-b to provider-a for eu-west. Rolling policy: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 5m checks. Using feature-flagged edge routing.

ops-bot: Route update queued: `edge route-set eu-west --weight provider-a=10 provider-b=90 --sticky true`

maya: monitoring at +1m: 10% shift done, errors on provider-b unchanged, provider-a latency stable. Proceeding to 30%.

ops-bot: Route update: `edge route-set eu-west --weight provider-a=30 provider-b=70 --sticky true`

ryan: provider-b error rate not improving. Observed increased CPU on provider-b's 4xx/5xx handlers. Suggest accelerating to 60%.

maya: advancing to 60% now.

ops-bot: Route update: `edge route-set eu-west --weight provider-a=60 provider-b=40 --sticky true`

sam: also toggling feature pack: disable long-context and reranker for standard and dev tiers. Command: `featureflag set eu-west long-context off --targets=standard,dev`

ops-bot: Feature flag updated: long-context=off (standard,dev). Reranker=off (standard,dev).

leah: support: enterprise customers still seeing intermittent 502s but much fewer. Informing Voxly that we're performing provider reroute and throttling standard tiers.

maya: at 60% shift p95 dropped from ~1.1s to 420ms, errors down from 3.9% to 1.2%. Proceed to 100% if trend holds.

sam: before full cutover, we should ensure provider-a can handle KV cache warming. Running: `cache warm --region eu-west --target provider-a --prefixes=active-tenants --parallel=8`

ops-bot: Cache warm job started (job id cw-5532). Estimated 90s.

ryan: watch memory usage on provider-a GPUs; we want to avoid OOM from cache pressure.

ops-bot: cw-5532 completed. No OOMs observed.

maya: advancing to 100% now.

ops-bot: Route update: `edge route-set eu-west --weight provider-a=100 provider-b=0 --sticky true`

sam: provider-b now at ~0 traffic, errors subsided platform-wide. Final checks: customer-visible errors back to baseline, latency stable.

leah: posted an interim customer note to Voxly and Chatly explaining temporary throttling and provider reroute, pointing to status.redwood.ai/incident/2101234567 (internal).

maya: one more mitigation: enabling a soft brownout for non-essential features globally in eu-west for 20 minutes to allow system to settle. `brownout set eu-west --features=rerank,codegen-extended --duration=20m --mode=soft`

ops-bot: Brownout applied.

ryan: deploybot shows no error regressions from provider-a path. Observability: traces show most long tails resolved.

sam: handing off to ryan for overnight monitoring. I'm shifting to secondary ops.

maya: thanks — handoff done. ryan, any special watch items?

ryan: watch p95 and 5xx on provider-a in eu-west, errors on the control-plane mesh (in case of hidden failback), and any customer escalations from enterprise tenants. If error rate climbs >0.5% alert immediately.

leah: support will keep an eye and escalate if enterprise customers see uptime impact. I’ll collect incident-affected customer list and estimated impact window.

maya: closing the page for active mitigation. Creating post-incident channel and assigning notes to postmortem owner sam.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation applied — provider reroute to provider-a, non-SLA throttles applied, soft brownout enabled. Status: Stabilized.

sam: creating follow-up: run a canary test to validate provider-b nodes before returning traffic. Also schedule a meeting with provider-b ops to review the driver rollback.

ryan: agreed. leaving monitoring watch. will escalate if anything changes.

maya: thanks team. After-action tasks: 1) postmortem (sam), 2) customer impact summary (leah), 3) provider root-cause call (alex + sam).

leah: noted. updating support doc and sending proactive emails.

maya: thread archived to incidents folder and I'll link it to the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
